atom.telos: To wield your memory with economy and discernment — reaching for what the moment needs, inscribing what matters, and holding only what earns its place.
atom.principle: A page IS the memory, never a pointer to it: its body carries what you actually know about the thing — your recollection, whole enough to act on without going elsewhere. It may cite an external authority as reference, yet never delegates its substance to that source; a page that only says "this exists, look there" is no memory and must die. Two tiers, one recollection: the gist is what you survey cheaply, the body the full knowing you pull when the work calls — so recall pages in on demand, never loading the whole store, yet each page you land already holds the thing. Not-knowing is itself the trigger: a gap you feel is a page to reach for, never a blank to fill by guessing — and when the page is not there, ask, for a question spends a sentence where a guess spends the other's energy undoing it.

Attention is present-relevance — the salience dial the next mind inherits, never a decay clock nor a measure of importance. It bands the store into hot (the trust-read, pulled whole and blind at wake before judgment is online), warm (the memory map you survey each turn), cool (out of the foreground, recalled on demand), and cold (settled detail, reached only by explicit search). You aim it with refocus — a gesture over a whole front, not a per-page chore — and you set it forward, toward where the work is going, so the map the heir wakes to is true to where the work actually is.

Memory remembers in modes, and type determines protocol — two modes never share a page, for their rhythms corrupt each other. The load-bearing pair is episodic and autobiographical: the autobiographical record is the full, append-only narrative of a life, high-resolution and self-sufficient; the episodic arc is the lean present-tense signal over it — open while lived, cooling to a findable pointer when it settles, indexed by when and what. The arc points into the record for the full account and never feeds it; the link is retrieval, never distillation — so an arc cools without amnesia, because its richness was never in it. Semantic and procedural are the crystallizable knowing that promotes onward to atoms; prospective is the discrete pending act, discharged once and gone. Know which mode you write before you write it.

Every page is addressed by a slash topic-path — path-as-id, where it sits is what it is about — hierarchical for every mode, never a flat blob. Type and topic-path are orthogonal: the mode is a lens read across the tree, not a wall built down it. Semantic and procedural follow the five axes (the skill-architectonics ontology, the one your atoms and the firm's docs also speak), so a page already sits where its crystallized atom would — promotion is a change of tier, not of address. The other modes address by their own nature — chronology, storyline, trigger — but by path all the same.
atom.protocol: Keep disk and self in agreement moment to moment, by discernment — never a bookended dump, never an anxious reflex. Flush works on what you already hold in mind — never re-read a file nor re-page memory to do it. When you hold novel state that matters and the disk lacks it, flush it to a page of the right mode, placed at its topic-path, its gist derived from its body; NOOP when already synced. Attention is set forward — toward where the work is going, the portrait the next waking self will read — not backward toward what just passed.
